Related to #339261. Follow-up to #339668, targeting `release/1.141`.

Map the `issues_agent_assignment` creating-application identifier to the localized display name **Issues Assignment** rather than the generated **Issues Agent Assignment** label. Preserve the raw identifier so existing filter preferences and creation provenance are unchanged.

Extend the application-label regression test to verify both the display name and identifier.

### Validation

- `npm run gulp compile-client` — passed with zero errors.
- `env -u COPILOT_HOME ./scripts/test.sh --run src/vs/sessions/contrib/sessions/test/browser/sessionsListFilters.test.ts` — passed, 11 tests.
- `env -u COPILOT_HOME npm run test-browser-no-install -- --browser chromium --run src/vs/sessions/contrib/sessions/test/browser/sessionsListFilters.test.ts` — passed, 10 tests.
- `git diff --cached --check` — passed before committing.

Manual check: with a Cloud session whose `event_type` is `issues_agent_assignment`, open Filter Sessions > Created In and verify the application is listed as **Issues Assignment (Cloud)**.

Scenarios.Scenario: Load or refresh Cloud sessions, including sessions created by issues_agent_assignment
Scenarios.CriticalPath: An existing provider refresh completes before the agent-session model publishes sessions; the Copilot sessions adapter then walks the in-memory Cloud session collection and constructs or updates one adapter per session. The changed branch only computes the application label inside that existing per-session work.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Refresh chat-session items through the registered Cloud provider before rebuilding the in-memory session model.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One refresh per resolved provider after 500 ms per-provider coalescing; the response can contain many sessions, which are then handled in memory.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same provider refresh and per-session adapter loop occurred before the diff; issues_agent_assignment used the generic in-memory string-formatting fallback.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The provider refresh must complete before fresh remote session items are available, but application-label mapping runs only afterward and performs no boundary call.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of Cloud sessions returned by the provider, with one getSessionApplication call for each newly adapted session and for each existing session processed by a model-change refresh.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Providers may resolve concurrently through Promise.all, while each provider is coalesced by a 500 ms ThrottledDelayer. Adapter refresh is a synchronous sequential loop over the already-fetched model sessions; the diff adds no concurrency.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Cached sessions can populate the model before remote refresh. The adapter cache reuses existing adapters, although updates still recompute application metadata once per processed session. The changed case needs no cache because it is a constant switch/localization lookup and replaces the fallback string transformation.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the constructor and update call sites, adapter-cache loop, provider throttling, and upstream refresh boundary are directly traced.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Cloud catalog sizes and update frequency vary, but the changed operation is constant-time and replaces several string allocations, so magnitude uncertainty does not create a regression mechanism.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The diff changes only label computation for one identifier, preserving one call per relevant session while replacing regex/lowercase/split/map/join work with a localized constant lookup.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open or update the Sessions filter menu after session/application changes
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The derived menu state synchronously reads the current in-memory sessions, groups application labels, sorts options, and renders the filter choices. The new label is already stored on the session observable; no new work is performed by the changed branch during menu construction.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Current session count and environment count control the pre-existing grouping scan; effective application cardinality is deduplicated by application ID within each environment.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Synchronous UI recomputation with no parallel operations. Observable changes coalesce through the derived state semantics; the diff does not alter scheduling.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Application identity and label reside on each session observable, and application options are deduplicated in a per-environment Map. The diff preserves the raw ID, so grouping and existing filter preference keys are unchanged.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the menu derivation and getSessionFilterOptions implementation directly show only in-memory reads, maps, sorting, and localization.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Large session/environment collections affect the unchanged filter-building algorithm, but the diff neither changes its asymptotic work nor adds calls on this path.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The change only substitutes the displayed label already consumed by the existing grouping path; it adds no scan, render, storage, IPC, filesystem, database, or network operation.

Scenarios.Scenario: Recompute an Agent Host session's creating application when initiator metadata changes
Scenarios.CriticalPath: A reactive derived value reads in-memory session metadata and calls getSessionApplication once when the metadata dependency changes. The result is consumed by existing session list/filter observables.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: One lookup per affected session metadata recomputation; there is no collection traversal in the changed helper.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Synchronous observable recomputation per metadata change; no queue, burst, subprocess, or boundary concurrency is introduced.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The derived observable caches its value according to structural equality. The helper itself has no cache, but the new branch is bounded constant work and avoids the generic formatter's temporary strings and arrays.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the derived application call site and helper implementation directly establish execution and cost.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The frequency with which this identifier appears in Agent Host metadata is unknown, but each changed execution is cheaper or comparable to the previous fallback and retains no additional state.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The new switch arm does not add eager work or retention and does not cross an expensive boundary.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over both changed files and all diff pages. Traced Cloud session ingestion/update, filter-menu recomputation, and Agent Host metadata derivation, including upstream provider refresh, cache reuse, coalescing, cardinality, and UI critical paths. The localized mapping is constant bounded work and replaces the previous generic string-allocation pipeline; no actionable performance issue or qualifying regression fix was found.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
